sections.summary:
SECTION: 1 Getting Started (Pages 5-18)

TOPICS: Wearing the watch, Charging, Pairing with phone, Button functions, Gesture controls, Watch face management, Favorite contacts, Workout monitoring

TEXT_EVIDENCE:
- The watch should be worn with the heart rate monitoring area on the top of the wrist, avoiding the joint, and neither too loose nor too tight (Page 5)
- Non-metallic straps with T-shaped buckles can be adjusted for a comfortable fit based on wrist circumference (Page 6)
- To remove a non-metallic strap, unlock the fastener, remove the current strap, and release the spring pin (Page 6)
- To remove a metal strap, follow the steps shown in Figure 2 (reverse order for installation) (Page 6)
- Leather straps are not water resistant; they should be kept dry and wiped clean promptly (Page 6)
- Step 1: Connect the USB Type-C port and power adapter, then plug in the power adapter (Page 7)
- Step 2: Rest the watch on the charging cradle, ensuring the contacts are aligned, and wait for the charging icon to appear (Page 7)
- Step 3: Charging stops automatically when the battery level reaches 100%, and it will restart if the battery drops below 100% while connected (Page 7)
- Use dedicated charging cable, cradle, and charger with 5 V output and 1 A or higher current (Page 8)
- Charging takes up to two hours; disconnect when the indicator shows 100% (Page 8)
- Do not charge in hazardous environments or near flammable materials (Page 8)
- Keep the charging cradle and contacts clean and dry to prevent short circuits (Page 8)
- The charging current is reduced if ambient temperature is low to protect battery lifespan (Page 8)
- There are three methods to check the battery level: on the charging screen, in the drop-down menu, or in the Huawei Health app (Page 9)
- To power on the watch, press and hold the Up button when it's powered off; it will also power on automatically if charged (Page 9)
- A critical low battery condition will cause the watch to remind the user to charge it and turn off after 2 seconds (Page 9)
- To power off the watch, press and hold the Up button and touch "Power off," or navigate through Settings > System > Power off (Page 9)
- To restart the watch, press and hold the Up button and touch "Restart," or use the same navigation path as powering off (Page 9)
- To force restart the watch, press and hold the Up button for at least 16 seconds (Page 9)
- The watch is ready to be paired via Bluetooth by default after startup (Page 10)
- Android users must download and install the Huawei Health app, which can be done by scanning the QR code or searching in AppGallery (Page 10)
- iOS users must ensure the device has been removed from the last device's list of paired devices and from Huawei Health before pairing (Page 10)
- Pairing involves touching "PAIR" in the Huawei Health app (Android) or selecting the watch in Bluetooth settings (iOS), followed by confirming on both devices (Page 10)
- The pairing process involves opening the Huawei Health app, navigating to Add > Smart Watch, and touching PAIR (Page 11)
- If pairing fails, the user should press the Down button and hold to unlock the watch and retry (Page 11)
- The watch can only be connected to one phone at a time; to pair with another, the current connection must be disconnected via the app (Page 11)
- Pressing the Up button wakes the screen and accesses the app list; pressing and holding powers on the watch or accesses the restart/power off screen (Page 11)
- Pressing the Down button opens the workout app and accesses customized features (Page 12)
- Pressing and holding the Down button locks/unlocks the screen and wakes up the voice assistant (Page 12)
- The lock/unlock feature is only available with HONOR MagicWatch Series, HONOR Watch VIVIERNE TAM version, HONOR Watch Magic/Dream Series, and HUWEI WATCH GT Series (Page 12)
- For the HONOR Watch GS Pro, the Up button is used to lock/unlock the screen, while the Down button switches screens during workouts (Page 12)
- The watch screen is locked by default during swim workouts and cannot be unlocked (Page 12)
- Voice assistant is only available with phones running EMUI 10.1 (Page 12)
- During a workout, pressing the Up button locks/unlocks, mutes, or ends the workout (Page 12)
- Pressing and holding the Down button wakes up the voice assistant, but this is currently only available with the HONOR Watch GS Pro (Page 12)
- The screen turns off automatically 5 seconds after turning on if no operation is performed; otherwise, it turns off 15 seconds after being turned on (Page 13)
- Users can enable the "Raise wrist to wake screen" function in the Huawei Health app (Page 13)
- The duration for the watch to go to sleep and turn off the screen can be adjusted in Settings > Display > Advanced, with a default setting of "Auto" (Page 13)
- Time and language settings do not need to be set manually on the watch as they are automatically synced from the connected phone (Page 13)
- Changes to language, time, or time format on the phone sync automatically to the watch when connected (Page 14)
- Ringtone adjustment is only available on HUAWEI WATCH GT 2 (46 mm), HONOR MagicWatch 2 (46 mm), and HONOR Watch GS Pro (Page 14)
- The ringtone for calls, alarms, and notifications is the default sound and cannot be customized (Page 14)
- To install a watch face, open the Huawei Health app, go to Watch faces > More, select a face, and touch Install (Page 14)
- To delete a watch face, open the Huawei Health app, go to Devices > Watch faces > Mine, select the face, and tap the trash icon in the upper-right corner (Page 14)
- A maximum of 10 favorite contacts can be added to the watch (Page 15)
- A maximum of 30 call records can be saved (Page 15)
- To set up favorite contacts, open the Huawei Health app, go to Devices, and touch Favorite contacts (Page 15)
- By default, pressing the Down button opens the Workout app (Page 15)
- To customize the Down button, go to Settings > Down button and select an app (Page 15)
- To choose Favorites apps, go to Settings > Display > Favorites and select desired apps like Transportation card, Sleep, Stress, Heart rate, Music, Weather, and Activity records (Page 15)
- To find your phone, press the Up button or swipe down on the home screen to access "Find my Phone" (Page 16)
- The phone will play a ringtone if it is within Bluetooth range, even in Silent mode (Page 16)
- The feature only works when the phone and watch are connected (Page 16)
- Method 1 for updating the watch involves connecting it to the phone via the Huawei Health app and selecting Firmware update (Page 16)
- For Android users, the Huawei Health app can be updated by touching Me and then Check for updates (Page 16)
- For iOS users, the Huawei Health app must be updated in the App Store (Page 16)
- The watch will automatically disconnect from the phone during an update (Page 17)
- The watch supports multiple workout modes (Page 18)
- The watch has preinstalled running courses from entry-level to advanced (Page 18)
- Users can choose different courses on their watch (Page 18)
- To start a workout, press the Up button, swipe to Workout, touch Running courses, and select a course (Page 18)
- During a workout, the Up button can be used to pause, end, lock the screen, or adjust volume (Page 18)
- After a workout, users can view detailed records including training effects, speed, steps, heart rate, and VO₂max (Page 18)
- For detailed workout data, open the Huawei Health app and touch Exercise records (Page 18)

- For Android users: Open Huawei Health app, touch Devices, touch device, touch Notifications, and enable Notifications (Page 29)
- For iOS users: Follow the same steps as Android users to enable notifications (Page 29)
- The watch will vibrate when a new message appears on the phone's status bar (Page 29)
- A maximum of 10 unread messages can be stored on the watch (Page 30)
- Only the latest 10 messages are displayed if there are more than 10 unread (Page 30)
- The watch can display messages from SMS, Email, Calendar, and various social media platforms (Page 30)
- Direct reply is not possible for SMS, WeChat, or email messages (Page 30)
- To delete a single message, swipe right; to delete all, touch Clear (Page 30)
- When connected to a phone, the watch vibrates and displays the caller's number and name for incoming calls (Page 30)
- Calls can be answered or rejected directly from the watch (Page 30)
- To make a call, press the Up button, swipe to find Contacts or Call Log, and select a contact (Page 30)
- The adding music feature is only supported on phones running Android 5.0 or later (Page 31)
- To add songs, open the Huawei Health app, go to Devices, select the device name, and touch Music (Page 31)
- For iOS users, connect the watch to an Android phone to add music, then reconnect to the iOS phone (Page 31)
- Music can be played through third-party social media apps, but only MP3 and AAC (LC-AAC) files can be added locally (Page 31)
- The watch can control music playback on a phone by enabling "Control phone music" in the Huawei Health app (Page 31)
- You can use the Huawei Health app to set a Smart alarm or an Event alarm (Page 32)
- The Smart alarm wakes you up during light sleep to make you feel more refreshed (Page 32)
- Method 1: Set an alarm using your watch by pressing the Up button, finding Alarm, and touching + (Page 32)
- Method 2: Set a Smart/Event alarm via the Huawei Health app, with specific steps for Android and iOS users (Page 32)
- If no repeat cycle is set, the alarm is a one-time alarm by default (Page 32)
- Working days (skip holidays) is not supported with alarms set on wearable devices (Page 32)
- Your device will currently only vibrate but not ring to inform you (Page 32)
- Event alarms can be synced to the Huawei Health app with a maximum of five alarms (Page 33)
- Only one Smart alarm can be set for the watch (Page 33)
- Alarms can be snoozed for 10 minutes by touching the screen, pressing the Up button, or swiping right (Page 33)
- The remote shutter feature requires EMUI 8.1 or Magic UI 2.0 and specific software versions for the Huawei Health app and watch models (Page 33)
- The stopwatch starts and resets with touch actions, and exits with a right swipe (Page 33)
- The timer offers eight default countdown modes: 1 minute, 3 minutes, 5 minutes, 10 minutes, 15 minutes, 30 minutes, 1 hour, and 2 hours (Page 33)
- The timer can be started, paused, and stopped by touching the screen (Page 34)
- The timer can be customized by setting a time on the Custom screen (Page 34)
- To use the flashlight, press the Up button, swipe to find Flashlight, and touch it (Page 34)
- The Barometer app measures altitude in the range of -800 to 8800 meters and air pressure from 300 to 1100 hPa (Page 34)
- Severe weather warnings are triggered when air pressure changes rapidly and exceeds a set value (Page 34)
- To enable severe weather warnings, go to Settings on the Air pressure screen within the Barometer app (Page 34)
- The compass is accessed by pressing the Up button, swiping to find "Compass," and following calibration instructions (Page 35)
- The wearable device's compass does not display longitude, latitude, or altitude; this information must be obtained from a phone (Page 35)
- The barometer of the wearable device can be used to view current altitude and air pressure (Page 35)
- There are three methods to check weather reports: on a watch face, on the weather screen, or in the Weather app (Page 35)
- To check weather on the watch, users must enable "Weather reports" in the Huawei Health app under Devices (Page 35)
- Users can set the temperature unit to Celsius °C or Fahrenheit °F (Page 35)
- For EMUI versions earlier than 9.0, the positioning mode should be set to "Use GPS, WLAN, and mobile networks" instead of "Use GPS only" (Page 35)
- The watch features a function to view outdoor environment information including sunrise, sunset, moonrise, moonset, moon phase, and tide times (Page 36)
- To access this, press the Up button to enter the app list, swipe on the screen, and touch Weather (Page 36)
- The watch can only display forecasts for the sunrise, sunset, moonrise, and moonset times for the next 5 days (Page 36)
- Tidal information is only available in some regions (Page 36)
- To enable Do Not Disturb mode, swipe down on the home screen, touch No Disturb, and then touch √ to confirm (Page 37)
- If the watch enters Do Not Disturb mode, it will not vibrate for incoming calls, but you can still answer or reject them (Page 37)
- Messages and notifications will not be displayed, and the Raise wrist to wake screen feature will be disabled (Page 37)
- Brightness is set to Auto by default, which automatically adjusts based on the environment (Page 37)
- Level 5 is the brightest setting and Level 1 is the dimmest setting (Page 37)
- If the watch does not support the calling feature, you will be unable to answer or reject incoming calls with the watch (Page 37)
